intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that ichthyosis with erythrokeratoderma (IEKD) is caused by heterozygous mutation in the gene encoding kallikrein-related peptidase 11 (KLK11).

checks.evidence_quote: We provide evidence that variants at Gly50 affecting the SP cleavage of KLK11 cause a new autosomal-dominant cornification disorder with abnormal desquamation.
checks.explanation: The abstract describes heterozygous KLK11 variants causing this disorder. 'IEKD' is the draft's name for it, not the paper's.

checks.explanation: The abstract names KLK11 as kallikrein-related peptidase 11.

paragraphs.text: Ichthyosis with erythrokeratoderma (IEKD) is an autosomal dominant Mendelian disorder of cornification. It starts early in life, with ichthyosiform erythroderma or erythrokeratoderma, and is associated with abnormal skin desquamation and a thickened, dense stratum corneum (Gong et al., 2023). Takeichi et al. (2023) described large hyperkeratotic pigmented plaques on the trunk as a feature of KLK11 ichthyosis.

paragraphs.text: Gong et al. (2023) studied 3 families with a previously undescribed cornification disorder: 1 familial case and 2 sporadic cases. The disorder was characterized by early-onset ichthyosiform erythroderma or erythrokeratoderma. The patients' stratum corneum was thickened and dense, which indicated abnormal skin desquamation. Ultrastructural study of the patients' stratum corneum showed delayed degeneration of corneodesmosomes.

paragraphs.text: Gong et al. (2023) performed whole-exome sequencing in 3 families with IEKD: 1 familial case and 2 sporadic cases. They identified 2 heterozygous mutations in the KLK11 gene, both affecting gly50, one of which was a gly50-to-glu (G50E) substitution. The mutations lay near the signal peptide cleavage site of KLK11. When overexpressed in eukaryotic cells, the mutations disrupted signal peptide cleavage. For the G50E variant, this led to mislocalization within the cell and reduced secretion from the cell. Trypsin-like and chymotrypsin-like proteolytic activity was significantly decreased in samples of the patients' stratum corneum. Proteolysis of desmoglein-1 was reduced, and corneodesmosomes degenerated more slowly, which indicated delayed skin desquamation.

paragraphs.text: Gong et al. (2023) used whole-exome sequencing to identify a heterozygous c.149G-A transition in the KLK11 gene, resulting in a gly50-to-glu (G50E) substitution near the signal peptide cleavage site, in patients with IEKD. The study included a familial case and 2 sporadic cases. In cell overexpression studies, the mutation disrupted signal peptide cleavage, causing the protein to be mislocalized within the cell and poorly secreted. The patients' stratum corneum showed reduced trypsin-like and chymotrypsin-like proteolytic activity, reduced desmoglein-1 proteolysis, and delayed degeneration of corneodesmosomes. Mice homozygous for the equivalent Klk11 mutation (G44E) had hyperkeratosis and abnormal desquamation.
